name: Memory
description: Memory (Concentration) is a domino adaptation of the card game Pelmanism. All double-6 tiles are laid face down in a 4×7 grid. On your turn you turn up two tiles; if they total 12 you remove them and take another turn; otherwise you turn them face down and the next player goes. The first to capture 50 tiles (25 pairs) or an agreed total wins. It is a test of memory.

history.origins: Concentration is an adaptation for dominoes of the card game Pelmanism, also known as Concentration or Memory. The card version originated in Europe; the domino version follows the same memory-matching principle with tiles laid in a grid. The game is also the basis for a popular American television quiz show using pairs of prizes.
timeline: Card game Pelmanism/Concentration established in Europe
Domino adaptation: tiles in grid, pairs total 12
Played by two or more players; first to 50 tiles wins

rules.objective: Be the first player to reach 50 captured tiles (25 pairs), or another predetermined total, by turning up pairs of tiles that total 12.
rules.gameplay: 1. Setup: all 28 tiles are placed face down in a 4×7 grid. 2. On your turn, expose any two tiles. If the pair totals 12, remove them from the grid and take another turn (continue until you fail to get a total of 12). If the pair does not total 12, turn them face down again and the next player takes a turn. 3. The hand is over when the grid is empty. 4. Winner is the first to reach 50 captured tiles (25 pairs) or the agreed total.
keyRules: Each turn: expose two tiles. If they total 12, remove them and go again; otherwise turn them face down and pass the turn.
Domino pairs that total 12: double-six with double-blank, 5-6 with 0-1; any seven (e.g. 1-6, 2-5, 3-4) pairs with any five (0-5, 1-4, 2-3) for nine combinations.
Game ends when grid is empty. First to 50 tiles (25 pairs) or agreed total wins.

strategy.basic: Remember which tiles appeared where when they were turned face down so you can form pairs that total 12 on your turn.
strategy.intermediate: Remember the total (12) and think in terms of pairs of values (e.g. 7 and 5) rather than the two halves of each tile.
strategy.advanced: Dominoes do not break into simple pairs like cards: double-blank and double-six pair only with each other; 0-1 and 5-6 pair only with each other. For 7+5 there are nine tile combinations (1-6, 2-5, or 3-4 with 0-5, 1-4, or 2-3); use this to plan which positions to reveal.
tips: Concentrate on the total 12 and the positions of turned-down tiles.
Avoid confusing the two ends of a tile; remember the sum each tile contributes.
When several tiles can make 12 with the same partner, track positions so you do not waste a turn on a wrong pair.
